To be fair, psychotropic medications are often used for treating depression that is resistant to the usual approach. A well-known (and well-advertised) one is Abilify, which is mainly prescribed as a supplement to SSRIs. BUT the weight gain from most of these augmenters is modest and, as such, could be feasibly controlled by diet. Plus Latuda, which is not associated with weight gain, is now on the market.

It's mostly the stronger psychotropics (which aren't approved for depression) that cause so much weight gain it can't necessarily be controlled; any normal weight person on these medicines has to be monitored for diabetes, high cholesterol, high blood pressure, etc.. because these are common side effects even if weight and diet do not change. TL:DR: Ethics taught in schools.

[rant] Long Version I believe that children should be taught ethics starting at 4 years old and continuing on as long as they are in school. We already do this is some fashion... Share, don't hit, don't put the cat in the microwave etc... but the field of ethics is deeply rich and has had some very insightful teachers ala Aristotle, Socrates, Confucius etc..

People often complain about the lack of real world education in schools. If we started ethical teaching at a young age and presented the same ideas but in more complicated scenarios as the kids got older you would eventually have a society of people who had engrained in them the core principles of what is essentially; be good to each other.

This society would grow over several generations to naturally root out what could only be described as corruption. Speaking as an American I can imagine a world where our politicians are back to "for the people" and the american dream is restored to the idea that you are free to pursue your goals instead of "society owes me."

The idea isn't without problems.

  • Who generates the curriculum?
  • How can you keep the content as agnostic as possible( though not a long term problem once the concepts set in )
  • If we have a limited curriculum what gets the cut?

Still, it's a novel idea. If an entire society had an understanding of how to apply ethics in even complicated social scenarios it would be possible to minimize federal and state laws because society as whole would recognize issues and address them. Very unrealistic to implement but fun to think about. [/rant]

Develop equatorial OTEC based marine farming facilities as a means to combat Global Warming.

OTEC is a well established solar power technology that has long languished because of its limited ability to scale and, like so many other solar energy technologies, it's most optimal locations are far from power markets. But as the 'engine' of other production rather than a 'power plant', using its full spectrum of output locally, it becomes commercially viable. OTEC plants not only generate power but a host of other resources including; cold for refrigeration, fresh water, nutrient-rich water, and various industrial gasses captured in what's called a 'degassing phase'. And so an OTEC can function as an engine for a broad spectrum of production including industrial scale polyspecies mariculture, industrial scale algaeculture, cold-bed agriculture, hydroponics farming, synthetic terra preta cultivation, methanol production, and other lesser products. There are also tourism possibilities as these complex could readily host resort facilities.

Additionally, an OTEC plant performs carbon sequester in exactly the same fashion as the wave-powered sea pumps once proposed by scientist James Lovelock, but with the powerful advantage of paying for itself. The nutrient-rich discharge of mixed surface and deep seawater stimulates a plume of algal growth which, in turn, stimulates the growth of salps that feed on algae. Salps are vertical migrators, rising to the surface at night to feed and sinking to the deep ocean where they excrete the remains of their meals as dense carbon pellets. At this depth, the waste doesn't re-enter the marine food cycle and simply falls as detritus to the sea floor. Thus this process harnesses a natural carbon sink in a moderate fashion while also stimulating a revitalization of regional fisheries in much the same way as natural upwelling zones. This combined with the carbon offset potential of the OTEC's many products makes it a powerful tool to combat Global Warming and restore our beleaguered oceans.

A complete OTEC facility (based on a 100MW plant) would be expensive--perhaps well over a billion dollars. However, its rich production would pay for it within two or three years while creating thousands of jobs per facility--and few other industries can boast that. Thus a venture could expand these complexes in an almost exponential manner, doubling their carbon offset and sequester impact every few years. In a couple of decades the entire current carbon output for our civilization could be compensated while at the same time ameliorating the global food crisis, obsolescing the old destructive fishing industry, and restoring the natural habitats that has ruined.
